scenes.section: The two IDs in this lesson

lines.raw: Claim number.
lines.say: Claim number.

lines.raw: Given by the **PBM** to each claim it receives.
lines.say: Given by the P B M to each claim it receives.

lines.raw: It identifies **one claim transaction**.
lines.say: It identifies one claim transaction.

lines.raw: Rx number (prescription number).
lines.say: Rx number (prescription number).

lines.raw: Given by the **pharmacy** to the prescription.
lines.say: Given by the pharmacy to the prescription.

lines.raw: It stays the **same for every refill**, like a file number.
lines.say: It stays the same for every refill, like a file number.

lines.raw: Two different pharmacies can use the same Rx number for different patients, so it is only unique **within one pharmacy**.
lines.say: Two different pharmacies can use the same Rx number for different patients, so it is only unique within one pharmacy.

lines.raw: Compound code.
lines.say: Compound code.

lines.raw: Says whether the drug is a normal **ready-made** product or a **compound**: a medicine the pharmacist mixes by hand from several ingredients.
lines.say: Says whether the drug is a normal ready-made product or a compound: a medicine the pharmacist mixes by hand from several ingredients.

lines.raw: Compounds are rare, but they are the one kind of pharmacy claim that lists several ingredients.
lines.say: Compounds are rare, but they are the one kind of pharmacy claim that lists several ingredients.

lines.raw: One claim, usually one drug.
lines.say: One claim, usually one drug.

lines.raw: A medical claim has a **header** (who, when, why) and **many lines** (one per service).
lines.say: A medical claim has a header (who, when, why) and many lines (one per service).

lines.raw: A pharmacy claim is much flatter: it usually covers **one drug, one fill**, so header and line are effectively one row.
lines.say: A pharmacy claim is much flatter: it usually covers one drug, one fill, so header and line are effectively one row.

lines.raw: If Emily picks up three medicines at once, the pharmacy sends **three separate claims**, and each gets its own answer.
lines.say: If Emily picks up three medicines at once, the pharmacy sends three separate claims, and each gets its own answer.

lines.raw: Here is a quick table.
lines.say: Here is a quick table.

lines.raw: One claim covers. Medical claim: A whole visit or stay. Pharmacy claim: **One drug, one fill**.
lines.say: One claim covers. Medical claim: A whole visit or stay. Pharmacy claim: One drug, one fill.

lines.raw: Lines. Medical claim: Many lines (one per service). Pharmacy claim: Usually just one.
lines.say: Lines. Medical claim: Many lines (one per service). Pharmacy claim: Usually just one.

lines.raw: Diagnosis on the claim? Medical claim: Yes, always. Pharmacy claim: Usually not.
lines.say: Diagnosis on the claim? Medical claim: Yes, always. Pharmacy claim: Usually not.

lines.raw: To count visits or fills. Medical claim: Count unique claim numbers. Pharmacy claim: Count claims, after removing cancelled ones (lesson 10).
lines.say: To count visits or fills. Medical claim: Count unique claim numbers. Pharmacy claim: Count claims, after removing cancelled ones (lesson 10).

lines.raw: Key code. Medical claim: CPT / HCPCS + ICD-10. Pharmacy claim: NDC.
lines.say: Key code. Medical claim: C P T or H C P C S and I C D 10. Pharmacy claim: N D C.

lines.raw: Why this matters for data.
lines.say: Why this matters for data.

lines.raw: Because one row is one fill of one drug, pharmacy data is the easiest claim data to count.
lines.say: Because one row is one fill of one drug, pharmacy data is the easiest claim data to count.

lines.raw: But the **Rx number alone** does not identify a prescription across the whole data set: always pair it with the **pharmacy's ID**.
lines.say: But the Rx number alone does not identify a prescription across the whole data set: always pair it with the pharmacy's I D.

lines.raw: Key takeaways.
lines.say: Key takeaways.

lines.raw: A pharmacy claim record turns one filled prescription into one row of fields.
lines.say: A pharmacy claim record turns one filled prescription into one row of fields.

lines.raw: Fields fall into groups: identity, drug, quantity and dates, prescriber and pharmacy, product choice, money and status.
lines.say: Fields fall into groups: identity, drug, quantity and dates, prescriber and pharmacy, product choice, money and status.

lines.raw: A pharmacy claim usually covers **one drug, one fill**, unlike multi-line medical claims.
lines.say: A pharmacy claim usually covers one drug, one fill, unlike multi-line medical claims.

lines.raw: The **claim number** identifies one claim; the **Rx number** identifies a prescription within one pharmacy and stays the same across refills.
lines.say: The claim number identifies one claim; the Rx number identifies a prescription within one pharmacy and stays the same across refills.
